title: Who the trial rules leave out
line: eligibility criteria applied to a national sample of real patients
question: If you apply a typical psychiatric trial's exclusion criteria to everyone in the country who has the disorder, how many real patients would have been allowed in?
data: NESARC or NSDUH national survey data
Hoertel et al. and Zimmerman et al. generalizability studies
planned: eligibility funnels drawn as an alluvial: everyone with the disorder enters on the left, each exclusion (comorbid substance use, suicidality, other psychiatric illness, medications) peels off a stream, and the thin trickle on the right is who a trial could enrol. small multiples for depression, bipolar disorder, panic and alcohol use disorder.

the anchor numbers are published: Zimmerman found most outpatients with depression would fail standard antidepressant-trial criteria, and Hoertel's group found 96.9% of treatment-seekers with alcohol dependence and a mood or anxiety disorder would be ineligible.
tie-in from the advocacy-and-accrual work: 52% of depression trials already exclude people with another psychiatric illness.
